full_judgment:
These Rules at the instance of the plaintiff-petitioner is directed against an order passed by Assistant Judge, Beanibazar Upazila on 8-2-88 in Miscellaneous Case No. 25 of 1986 rejecting the application under Order 5 rule 20 of the Code of Civil Procedure and the Miscellaneous Case under Order 9 rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure for restoration of the original Title Suit No. 265 of 1972 and also the order dated 7-4-88 rejecting the application under section 151 of the Code for restoration of the Miscellaneous Case after setting aside the order dated 8-2-88. 

 2. The short facts relevant is that, the petitioner and proforma opposite party Nos. 15 and 16 being plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 265 of 1972 for declaration of their title and for permanent injunction with a prayer for temporary injunction restraining the defendants from interfering with their peaceful possession and enjoyment in the suit land. The suit while thus proceeding in view of the government policy different Munsifs courts were established at thana level in new conception of upazila. On 18-5-86 plaintiff No. 1 came to the court of Munsif, Beanibazar Upazila in connection with another case and came to learn for the first time that the title suit aforesaid was transferred from Sylthet Sadar to Beanibazar and was dismissed for default on 24-4-86. Prior to that plaintiffs had no knowledge about the transfer of the suit from the 1st court of Musif, Syhlet to Beanibazar Upzila. Accordingly, on 21.5.86 the plaintiffs filed an application under Order 9 rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure being Miscellaneous Case No. 25 of 1986 for restoration of the suit after setting aside the dismissal order. 

 3. After filing the Miscellaneous Case for restoration the tabdirkar was taking proper steps. The notices of the said Miscellaneous Case were duly served on defendant opposite parties Nos. 1-3, 6-10, and 12 and at the order of the learned court dated 22-9-87 the petitioners issued notice under registered card with A/D and deposited the postal receipts on 19-12-87 in court. As some of the defendants refused to accept the notice those were returned unserved and accordingly the learned court on 21-1-88 directed the plaintiffs to take proper steps for service of notice on them. On that date the plaintiff petitioners took time and subsequently on 8-2-88 filed an application under Order 5 rule 20 of the Code of Civil Procedure for substituted service of summons upon the defendant opposite parties on whom the notices could not be served. The learned Assistant Judge by his impugned order dated 8-2-88 rejected the application on the ground that the application was not supported by affidavit and also rejected the Miscellaneous Case under Order 9 rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure for restoration on a finding that no steps regarding service of notice has been taken as per order of the court. 

 4. Then the plaintiff petitioners filed an application under section 115 of the Code for restoration of the Misecllaneous case after setting aside the order dated 8-2-88. The Assistant Judge after hearing rejected the same by his order dated 7-4-88. 

 6. Mr. M A Tariq, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners, submits that the application for substituted service of summons does not require any affidavit save and except verification which was very much there but the learned Assistant Judge committed an illegality in rejecting the application on the ground that it was not supported by affidavit. Mr. Tariq makes serious grievance against the impugned orders and submits that the learned trial Court committed serious illegality in rejecting the Miscellaneous Case while rejecting the application for substituted service of summons in total disregard of the provisions of law in this regard and, as such, the impugned orders are liable to be set aside. There is substance in the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner. 

 8. On perusal of the record it appears that the learned Assistant Judge rejected the application under Order 5 rule 20 of the Code of Civil Procedure on wrong conception of law that it was not supported by any affidavit where only verification is required. It further appears that he while rejecting the application for substituted service of summons rejected the Miscellaneous Case under Order 9 rule 9 of the Code illegally in total violation of the provisions of law in this regard which cannot be sustained in law and is liable to be set aside. The application under section 151 of the Code filed by the plaintiff-petitioners was a misconceived one. 

 11. The trial Court is further directed to dispose of the Miscellaneous Case in accordance with law positively within 2 (two) months from the date of receipt of this order. Communicate the order to the court concerned at once.
